text:
alex: FYI — saw two node preemptions during the canary at ~09:05, runtime auto-routed to fallback variant and we got a latency bump.
priya: which fallback path kicked in? variant fallback or regional failover?
alex: variant-fallback first, then regional after health checks failed for that zone. deploy-bot reported: Canary progress 5% -> 10% -> fallback triggered.
deploy-bot: Canary 1715009876: stage=canary percent=10 event=fallback_triggered reason=preempt_detected
jamie: are we sure the console UI shows which fallback path was used? customers asked for clearer telemetry.
priya: current telemetry tags: rollout_id, fallback_type, triggered_by, and runtime_node_id. But UI groups them under "rollout events" — not super visible.
alex: proposing small change: show a per-route fallback badge in the rollout timeline with hover details including node id, latency delta, and exact traffic fraction diverted.
jamie: agree. Also we should cap automatic fallback percent during preemption to avoid thrashing. suggested: max_fallback_percent=15 and backoff window=120s.
priya: +1 but we need a safety leash for A/B as well — if variant fallback causes quality regression we should auto-revert to baseline rather than keep falling through regions.
alex: good point. add quality signal to decision: if eval_metric_drop > 3% within 5m, escalate to manual rollback and notify oncall.
jamie: implementation sketch for runtime policy:
```
policy {
  trigger: node_preempt | zone_unhealthy
  fallback_order: ["variant-lite","regional-serve","degrade-mode"]
  max_fallback_percent: 15
  quality_check: { metric: "resp_f1", window_s: 300, threshold_pct: 3 }
  backoff_s: 120
}
```
priya: console UX: add toggle for auto-fallback (on/off), and a quick "safety profile" dropdown: permissive / conservative / strict which maps to max_fallback_percent and backoff.
jamie: need telemetry changes: emit fallback_event with fields: rollout_id, fallback_order, percent_diverted, preempting_node, latency_p50_before, latency_p50_after, quality_signal_delta. also include a dedup key so alerts don't spam.
sre-bot: alert: fallback-spike for rollout 1715009876 — percent_diverted=10 latency_p95_delta=540ms
alex: thanks all. action items: priya will spec UI changes + safety profiles, jamie will add telemetry fields and dedup key, i'll update runtime policy with quality gating and backoff. oncall to watch next canary.
priya: will draft console mockups and a short API change set for rollout policy by EOD.
jamie: I'll add telemetry proto and a lightweight alert rule that groups by rollout_id and dedup_key. want to test against replayed events.
alex: one more: should we allow a per-customer override for fallback aggressiveness? e.g., enterprise customers might prefer stricter fallbacks.
priya: yes but default should remain conservative. add tenant_override: boolean with audit log requirement.
alex: cool. if nothing else i'll kick a PR for the runtime change tomorrow morning and include the sample policy above.
jamie: 👍
deploy-bot: Canary 1715009876: status=paused awaiting-manual-ack after quality-check-failure (eval_drop=3.4%)
alex: closing loop — that's expected per new quality gate. oncall please ack and coordinate rollback if necessary.
sre-bot: acknowledged. assigning incident channel #incidents/1715009876 for postmortem tracking."
